What to check before buying business software

A requirements-first checklist for evaluating business software, licensing and implementation.

Before comparing software, describe the business process it needs to support. Identify the users, approvals, information and exceptions involved.

What to consider

Review data import and export, integrations, access roles, reporting and licensing. Ask how updates, support, backups and account access work.

A trial or demonstration can help verify important workflows, but use realistic scenarios. Note which requirements are essential and what needs configuration.

Document ownership, implementation effort, training needs and recurring costs before deciding. Adoption and ongoing administration matter too.
